I2 not met: functional acquisition used only 18 axial slices covering the parietal lobe and most prefrontal cortex, explicitly excluding the orbitofrontal sector; no whole-brain analysis is demonstrated. Mental subtraction meets I1, gradient-echo EPI task activation meets I4, and Table 1 reports standardized activation coordinates (I3). Ten healthy adults have group task-versus-control effects. Although pairwise task comparisons use a parietal search region, Table 1 reports effects across the acquired volume, so E1 is not met. E2-E4 do not apply.

Results include healthy-group task effects and are not limited to ROI or between-group comparisons; E1–E4 do not apply.

Single-subject fMRI case study of one healthy 21-year-old man. It provides no group-level healthy-adult analysis or healthy-group task effect (I2 not_met; E3 met). Detour planning and Tower of London satisfy I1; whole-volume planning-versus-nonplanning BOLD analyses and Talairach activation coordinates satisfy I3 and I4. Results are original individual task effects, not ROI-only or disease, age, or gender comparisons (E1, E2, E4 not_met).

I2 not_met: an initial whole-brain screen is described, but a qualifying whole-brain healthy-group task effect is not demonstrated. Table 2 reports sighted-control MAZE-REST peaks only within predefined 10-mm spherical search volumes using ROI/small-volume correction. The additional intraparietal coordinate concerns a group-by-run interaction, not an independently reported whole-brain healthy-group task contrast. E1 remains unclear because the search volume for that interaction is unspecified. Tactile maze solving with adult sighted controls, MNI activation coordinates, and BOLD fMRI establish I1, I3 and I4. Within-control task effects and original human data mean E2, E3 and E4 do not apply.

Original BOLD fMRI study of arithmetic word-problem solving in 36 healthy adults, with whole-brain group-level regressions (I1, I2, I4 met). However, Tables 3 and 4 report only MNI peaks for between-participant correlations of task activation with visualization or verbalization scores. No healthy-group task activation increase or within-group task-condition effect is demonstrated (I3 not_met; E3 met). The positive cognitive-style associations do not establish a group task activation effect.

E3 met: participants were randomly assigned to separate HFF and OHFF groups, and the only reported voxelwise contrast (Table 1) compares correct HFF resolution with incorrect OHFF resolution. No within-group healthy task activation contrast is reported. I1-I4 are otherwise met: scientific problem solving, healthy adults aged 20–25, whole-brain group-level BOLD analysis, and Talairach activation peaks. E1, E2 and E4 do not apply.

Healthy-group task contrasts are present; E2-E4 do not apply.
